notes.summary: Primary-source audit: local all-ideal/divisorial foundations verified, operator conventions converted, and the BMP recovery theorem used only as the supplied premise.
notes.detailedSummary: Indispensable passages were retrieved from Xia–Zhang, Boucksom, BFJ, Guan–Zhou, Darvas–Xia and Witt Nyström. Exact local hypotheses and exponential conventions are recorded. Direct downloads failed; successful browser passages and failures are preserved. The unread Demailly PDF is not used as a premise. Symbolic checks verify two algebraic identities, not the analytic proofs.
notes.text:
This is a primary-source audit. The task supplies the original BMP recovery theorem and smooth gauge theorem as premises. No earlier notes are supplied.

Throughout, D=dd^c=(i/(2π))∂bar∂ and d^c=(i/(4π))(bar∂−∂). Write ν_E(w) for the coefficient of log|f_E|² in the generic logarithmic singularity of the canonical pullback of w. Thus ν_E(log|f|²)=ord_E(f). Sources measuring growth relative to log|z| have Lelong number 2ν_E(w). In particular the task's I(tw) is Boucksom's and BFJ's J(tw/2), since their J(φ) uses exp(−2φ).

The indispensable local statements retrieved from Boucksom, https://sebastien.boucksom.perso.math.cnrs.fr/notes/L2.pdf, are Definition 9.2 and Theorem 9.3, Theorem 9.17, §10.1, the sum/max formulae preceding Proposition 10.6, and Theorem 10.13 with Corollary 10.15. The complete PDF repeatedly timed out; these exact primary-source passages were retrieved through search indexing. In task conventions the resulting local criterion is:

For a nonzero holomorphic germ f at x and t>0, f belongs to I(tw)_x if and only if there exists δ>0 such that
ord_E(f)+A(E)≥(1+δ)tν_E(w)
for every prime divisor over a sufficiently small neighborhood whose center contains x. Here A(E)=1+ord_E(K_{Y/U}). One δ must work for every E. Separately strict inequalities without a uniform margin are not substituted. The theorem concerns local quasi-psh functions on smooth complex manifolds. It requires neither a closed background nor BMP; its analytic comparison weight is log|f|. Bounded smooth additions preserve integrability and logarithmic growth.

Strong openness was checked directly in Guan–Zhou, Annals 182 (2015), §1.2 and Theorem 1.1, https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v182-n2-p05-p.pdf. This source uses exp(−φ), as in the task. Its negative-psh-polydisc hypotheses apply locally after adding a smooth quadratic function, shrinking the chart and subtracting a constant. These bounded changes leave the relevant ideals unchanged.

BFJ, https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0702487v2, Theorem A, Theorem 5.5 and equation (5.3), provide an independent local check of the all-weight equivalence. Their statements initially use J_+; Guan–Zhou supplies J_+=J. Their growth and exponential conventions require the factor conversion above. No numerical normalization of their geometric dd^c is inferred for these growth-based applications.

Darvas–Xia, Geometry & Topology 28 (2024), Proposition 2.2 and Lemma 3.1, were retrieved in the published text hosted at https://research.chalmers.se/publication/542539/file/542539_Fulltext.pdf. The text uses D=(i/(2π))∂bar∂ and exp(−tu). Its global setting is compact Kähler with closed background; §3 assumes a big cohomology class. Its initial envelope uses all-ideal inclusion. The identification with the task's equality envelope is proved in n3. Lemma 3.1 is used only at the exact closed pulled background and its argument is reconstructed in n8. The proposed Demailly Trieste PDF could not be retrieved; the needed integrability transformation is instead proved by change of variables.

Witt Nyström, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1703.01950v1, Theorem 1.2, supplies ordinary-singularity mass monotonicity for arbitrary singularities on a compact Kähler manifold. Closedness is indispensable: its proof locally uses θ=dd^cρ. We apply it only to κ on P². The retrieved v1 does not explicitly specify the numerical operator constant; simultaneous positive rescaling of background and potentials transfers its conclusion to the task's convention. Its §2 also states the positivity, multilinearity and absence of pluripolar mass used for closed non-pluripolar products. No ambient nonclosed mass monotonicity is used.

Xia–Zhang, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.21053v1, uses i∂bar∂, the inverse generator e^(−1), and a background equal to 2πh here. The inverse generates the same quotient group. Sections 2–4 were retrieved, including the heat estimates, transport, cutoff, scalar correction and final strictness check. Their entire indispensable threefold construction is independently reconstructed in n2; no extension to other dimensions is inferred.

Artifacts: input.json preserves the supplied input. retrieve.py, retrieval.json and retrieval.log preserve direct-download attempts and their PermissionError failures. sources/browser_capture_1.jsonl and sources/browser_capture_2.json through sources/browser_capture_14.json preserve successful browser passages and failures. audit_checks.py and audit_output.json preserve the symbolic checks and environment: Python 3.12.14, SymPy 1.14.0, Linux x86_64. Rerun with python audit_checks.py; repeat direct retrieval with python retrieve.py. Browser retrieval can be repeated using the URLs and theorem searches above. No supervised heavy-compute facility was exposed; none was needed or used. The symbolic outputs are a completed-square residual of 0 and a converted mass coefficient of 6. They do not establish analytic correctness.

notes.summary: A proved: the prescribed Hopf threefold has the claimed geometry and metric, and actual smooth strict h-potentials have divergent mass.
notes.detailedSummary: The quotient is smoothly S⁵×S¹ and fibers elliptically over P² with the specified scalar action. The normalized metric satisfies dh=−ds∧α and has smooth mass 6+6 times fiber energy. A fully specified heat transport, cutoff and scalar correction produces globally smooth strict potentials with divergent fiber energy. Only the threefold construction is proved.
notes.text:
Proof of A, reconstructing the indispensable construction audited in n1.

The maps z↦e^kz act freely and properly discontinuously on C³\{0}: only finitely many k move one compact radial annulus to meet another. Polar coordinates identify the smooth quotient with S⁵×(R/Z), using log|z| modulo 1. Thus it is smooth, compact and connected. Its inherited complex charts make it a complex threefold.

Projectivization descends. On z₀≠0 write ξ=(z₁/z₀,z₂/z₀) and z₀=e^w. The fiber coordinate is w modulo Z+2πiZ; changes of base chart translate w by a local holomorphic logarithm. These charts establish the holomorphic submersion π:X→P² with connected elliptic fibers. Scalar multiplication e^t gives the free E=C/(Z+2πiZ) action, transitive on each fiber.

The function s=log|z|² does not descend, since it changes by 2k. Its differentials and the forms α=Ds and β=ds∧d^cs descend and are E invariant. In the chart, s=w+bar w+ρ, where ρ=log(1+|ξ|²), and
α=(i/(2π))∂bar∂ρ=π*κ,
β=(i/(2π))(dw+∂ρ)∧(dbar w+bar∂ρ).
This is the Fubini–Study normalization ∫κ²=1. The kernel of α is vertical and β is positive on the vertical line, proving h=α+β is positive definite. Direct differentiation gives
dh=−ds∧α≠0, Dβ=−α², α³=β²=0, D(h²)=0.
Nonvanishing follows by testing one radial and two transverse real directions. The background h is big, with strict potential 0.

Let dA_E=(i/(4π))dw∧dbar w, with integral 1 over E. For smooth real V, integration by parts gives
∫_X(h+DV)³=∫h³+3∫dV∧d^cV∧α²
=6+6∫_{P²}(∫_E|V_w|²dA_E)κ².                 (1)
The linear term vanishes by D(h²)=0, and the cubic exact term integrates to zero. The quadratic term is −3∫Vα²∧DV. On each fiber β=2dA_E, so ∫h³=6. All constants therefore match the task's operator.

For V=V(x,w), x=log|ξ|² and μ=e^x/(1+e^x), a transverse angular/radial/vertical frame gives the Hermitian matrix of 2π(h+DV). Its angular entry is (μ+V_x)/μ; its remaining block has entries
(μ+V_xx)/(μ(1−μ)), (μ+V_xbarw)/sqrt(μ(1−μ)),
(μ+V_wx)/sqrt(μ(1−μ)), 1+V_wbarw.
Consequently strictness is exactly
1+V_wbarw>0, μ+V_x>0,
Q[V]:=V_xx+μ−|μ+V_xbarw|²/(1+V_wbarw)>0.       (2)
A function independent of x at the negative end and constant in both variables at the positive end extends smoothly across ξ=0 and across the complement of a compact subset of this affine chart.

Here is the actual family. For Λ=Z+2πiZ and 0<η<1/10 define
k_t(w)=(2/t)Σ_{l∈Λ}exp(−|w−l|²/t),
F_η(t,w)=−η∫_t^∞(k_r(w)−1)dr.
Gaussian lattice sums and their derivatives converge on t≥t₀>0. Unfolding gives ∫k_t dA_E=1. With ν_{p,q}=p+iq/(2π), Fourier expansion gives
k_t=Σ exp(−π²|ν|²t)exp(2πip Re w+iq Im w),
F_η=−(η/π²)Σ_{ν≠0}exp(−π²|ν|²t)|ν|^(−2)exp(2πip Re w+iq Im w).
Therefore
F_t=F_wbarw=η(k_t−1), 1+F_wbarw>1−η,
||∂_t^aF_η||_{C^m}≤C_{a,m}η exp(−t/4), t≥1.  (3)
The heat equation is ∂_tk_t=∂w∂barw k_t. Gaussian probability weights yield
(log k_t)_wbarw=−1/t+Var(w−l)/t²≥−1/t.          (4)
Parseval gives E_η(t)=η²π^(−2)Σ_{ν≠0}exp(−2π²|ν|²t)/|ν|² and E_η'(t)=−2η²(k_{2t}(0)−1). Since k_{2t}(0)=1/t+O(t^(−1)exp(−c/t)), integration from t to 1 proves
E_η(t)=2η²log(1/t)+O(η²), 0<t≤1,              (5)
uniformly in η,t.

For 0<t≤1 put G=|t∂barw log k_t|. Choosing a nearest lattice point at distance d gives k_t≤Ct^(−1)exp(−d²/t) and G≤C(d+exp(−1/(Ct))). Factor out the nearest Gaussian; the other lattice distances have uniformly summable tails, and when d<1/4 the other points are uniformly separated. Splitting according to whether G exceeds twice the exponential error gives
tk_t≤C₀exp(−G²/(C₀t)).                        (6)
Fix K>0 with C₀K<1/200. For H=ηk_t, 1/2≤μ≤1, σ²=(2K/η)log(1/(ηt)), and ζ=(σt/μ)∂barw log k_t,
Ktk_t−μ²(1−η)H/(1−η+H)|ζ−1/(1−η)|²
≤CK exp(−1/(Cσ²t)).                          (7)
If σ²t≥1/100, use tk_t≤C₀. Otherwise, when the displayed distance is ≥1/4, the square term is ≥H/[100(1+H)], while Kt(1+H)<η/100, making the left side nonpositive. In the remaining case |ζ|≥3/4, hence G≥3/(8σ), and (6) proves the exponential bound. The argument also works for smaller positive K.

Set ε_η=η^(1/η²), q₀=sqrt(log(1/(ηε_η))), A_η=sqrt(K/(2η)). Choose a smooth increasing χ, zero on (−∞,0], one on [1,∞), with ∫₀¹χ=1/2. Define
q(x)=q₀−∫₀^{A_ηx}χ(y)dy,
t(x)=η^(−1)exp(−q(x)²),
b_η=(q₀−1/2)/A_η, x*_η=(q₀+1/2)/A_η.
Then t=ε_η for x≤0, q(b_η)=1, q(x*_η)=0, and b_η,x*_η=O(sqrt(log(1/η)/η)). Choose a smooth transition θ_cut from 0 to 1 on [0,1], constant outside, and put
W_η(x,w)=θ_cut(q(x))F_η(t(x),w).
It equals F_η(ε_η,w) for x≤0 and 0 for x≥x*_η; its vertical positivity is >1−η.

For q≥1, set σ=(log t)_x and H=ηk_t. Expansion of (2) gives
Q[W]=σ²t{H[1+t(log k_t)_wbarw]−η}
+σ_xt(H−η)+μ(1−μ)−μ²η/(1−η)
+μ²(1−η)H/(1−η+H)|(σt/μ)∂barw log k_t−1/(1−η)|². (8)
The exact symbolic residual checked by audit_checks.py is zero.

On 0≤x≤A_η^(−1), σ=2A_ηqχ and σ_x=−(K/η)χ²+(K/η)qχ'. The time is smaller than every fixed power of η. Equations (4),(7), with Kχ² replacing K, imply [Q[W]]_-≤Cη: the χ' contribution is ≥−Kqχ't≥−η, and σ²t≤η². If χ=0, χ'=0 and Q>0 directly. On A_η^(−1)≤x≤b_η, σ=2A_ηq and σ_x=−K/η. For t≤1,
[Q[W]]_-≤2η+2Kq²t+CK exp(−η/(CKq²t));
for t≥1, (3) gives [Q[W]]_-≤CKq²t²exp(−t/4).

Let d_η(x)=max_w[Q[W_η]]_-. These bounds have integral o(1). Indeed dx=−dq/A_η and t=η^(−1)e^(−q²). The q²t contribution is O(sqrt(η log(1/η))). Split the exponential contribution at 2sqrt(log(1/η)); the initial length is O(sqrt(log(1/η))), while the remaining integral is bounded using η²e^(q²)/q²≥e^(q²/4), then multiply by A_η^(−1)=O(sqrt η). For t≥1 use dx=sqrt(η/(2K))dt/(tq) and integrability of t exp(−t/4). Constant errors contribute O(ηb_η)=o(1).

Also sup[W_x]_- =O(sqrt(η log(1/η)))=o(1), from W_x=σtη(k_t−1) for t≤1 and (3) thereafter. On b_η≤x≤x*_η, t≥1/(eη), so |W_x|+|Q[W]−Q[0]|≤Cexp(−1/(5eη)). This is o(exp(−x*_η)), whereas Q[0]=μ(1−μ)≥exp(−x*_η)/4. Thus Q[W]>0 there. It is positive for x≤0, since Q≥μ(1−μ/(1−η)), and for x≥x*_η. Therefore d_η is continuous, supported in [0,b_η], and has integral o(1). On [−2,−1], Q[W]≥2/27.

Choose a smooth nonnegative majorant r_η supported in (−1/2,b_η+1/2), strictly above d_η on [0,b_η], with m_η=∫r_η≤∫d_η+η=o(1). Smoothing and a small positive excess construct it. Fix a smooth probability bump p supported in (−2,−1), and define
g_η(x)=∫_{−∞}^x(x−y)(r_η(y)−m_ηp(y))dy,
V_η=W_η+g_η.
Then −m_η≤g_η'≤0, and g_η is zero at the negative end and constant at the positive end. Moreover Q[V_η]=Q[W_η]+r_η−m_ηp>0: the majorant fixes [0,b_η], and the negative correction is absorbed by 2/27 on its disjoint support. The slopes vanish for x≤−2; thereafter μ≥μ(−2) and all negative slopes are o(1), proving μ+(V_η)_x>0. Vertical positivity remains >1−η. Equation (2) proves global smooth strictness.

On the fixed ball |ξ|²<e^(−3), V_η=F_η(ε_η,w), whose fiber energy is 2log(1/η)+O(η²) by (5). Equation (1) proves divergent mass. Taking any sufficiently small sequence η_j↓0 gives actual smooth strict potentials φ_j=V_ηj; subtracting their suprema normalizes them without changing currents. Thus v_+(h)=∞. The construction proves precisely the threefold case and the prescribed operator/background.

notes.summary: General B proved for arbitrary smooth backgrounds: exact equality envelopes, finite-maximum Hessian closure, all exceptional constraints, retraction and canonical limits.
notes.detailedSummary: A feasible normalized seed makes the equality envelope nonempty. It equals the envelope defined by inequalities at every local divisorial valuation. Finite maxima and Choquet limits retain those constraints via canonical L¹ convergence on modifications. Exact ideals, normalization, idempotence and ordered-background composition follow. Fixed feasible ideal data have metric-independent decreasing limits without BMP.
notes.text:
Proof of the general part of B. Every divisor here includes prime divisors on arbitrary smooth local modifications, not only divisors on the original compact manifold. Use n1's local conventions and verified premises.

Exact all-weight ideal equivalence is equivalent to equality of every ν_E. Equality of orders implies equality of ideals by n1's uniform-margin criterion. Conversely, for every integer m≥1,
ν_E(w)−A(E)/m≤ord_E I(mw)/m≤ν_E(w).           (9)
The lower bound is the necessary integrability inequality applied to local generators. The upper bound follows from the qualitative approximation theorem: (m/2)w is more singular than log|I(mw)|, hence w≤m^(−1)log Σ|g_i|²+O(1). Pulling back proves the upper order bound. Therefore the ideals for m→∞ determine every order. These arguments apply to quasi-psh weights after bounded smooth additions. They also show that ν_E(w)≥ν_E(u) for all E is equivalent to I(tw)⊆I(tu) for all t>0.

Finite maxima lose no smooth background. For smooth w_i set F_δ=δ log Σexp(w_i/δ), p_i=exp(w_i/δ)/Σexp(w_k/δ). Direct differentiation gives
θ+DF_δ=Σp_i(θ+Dw_i)
+(1/δ)Σp_i d(w_i−F_δ)∧d^c(w_i−F_δ).          (10)
The covariance terms are positive and the coefficient of θ is exactly one. Closedness is not used. For genuine θ-psh functions, local convolution gives Dw_{i,ε}≥−θ_ε, where θ_ε→θ uniformly on smaller charts. Apply (10), then pass to the local smooth limit and δ↓0. The result is θ+Dmax_iw_i≥0 exactly. The maximum is genuine at poles. The checked local growth formulae give
ν_E(max_iw_i)=min_iν_E(w_i),
ν_E(Σt_iw_i)=Σt_iν_E(w_i) for t_i≥0.          (11)

Let u∈PSH(M,θ), sup u=0, on a compact connected complex manifold. The task's competitor class contains u. Its usc supremum U lies between u and 0. Adding one smooth strongly psh function locally provides a common psh bound. Choquet's lemma and finite maxima with u produce competitors U_j increasing almost everywhere to U. Their canonical usc limit is genuine θ-psh and not identically −∞. Since u≤U≤0, sup U=0.

Exceptional constraints require an additional check. For any smooth local modification μ:Y→V⊂M, U_j∘μ are genuine, uniformly quasi-psh locally, and between u∘μ and 0. They converge in L¹_loc to U∘μ. Local quasi-psh compactness applies; the fixed integrable lower bound prevents collapse. Every convergent subsequence agrees with U∘μ on the isomorphism locus, where local L¹ convergence transports biholomorphically. The exceptional set has Lebesgue measure zero, so this identifies the whole limit and its canonical representative. At a very general point of E chosen simultaneously for the countable sequence and its limit, Lelong upper semicontinuity gives
ν_E(U)≥limsup_jν_E(U_j)=ν_E(u).
The opposite inequality follows from U≥u. Thus every local exceptional order is retained. The local criterion proves I(tU)=I(tu) for all real t>0. Consequently U is itself a competitor and its ideal class has the identical competitor set; P_θ[U]_I=U.

Increasing canonical potentials need not converge pointwise to their usc supremum at every pole. The statement proved above is canonical L¹ pullback convergence and equality after usc regularization. Noncollapsed decreasing sequences in a common local quasi-psh class, in contrast, converge pointwise everywhere to a genuine representative, and their compositions with modifications have exactly the same canonical pointwise limit. No general continuity of decreasing-sequence Lelong numbers is claimed.

The equality envelope also equals the usc supremum of all normalized θ-psh w satisfying ν_E(w)≥ν_E(u) for every local E. Indeed max(w,u) has exact seed orders by (11), hence exact seed ideals by (9), and dominates w. This identifies the task's equality envelope with the inclusion envelope used in Darvas–Xia. The same pullback closure argument preserves every inequality.

If θ₁≤θ₂ and u is θ₁-psh, P_{θ₁}[u]_I retains exactly u's ideals, so the two θ₂ competitor sets coincide:
P_{θ₂}[P_{θ₁}[u]_I]_I=P_{θ₂}[u]_I.           (12)
Order inequalities between seed data give corresponding envelope inequalities. Convex combinations and (11) give
λP_θ[u₁]_I+(1−λ)P_θ[u₂]_I
≤P_θ[λu₁+(1−λ)u₂]_I.                        (13)
More generally a pointwise concave decreasing feasible seed family has concave decreasing envelopes: convex combinations of competitors have every order at least that of the interpolated seed, so the inequality-envelope description applies. This checks all real weights and all local divisors.

Fixed feasible ideal data have exact decreasing limits without BMP. For any positive Hermitian g let W_j=P_{θ+g/j}[u]_I. These decrease and satisfy u≤W_j≤0. Their genuine θ-psh limit W has canonical decreasing pullbacks. Semicontinuity and W≥u imply ν_E(W)=ν_E(u), since each W_j has that order. Thus W≤P_θ[u]_I, while every W_j≥P_θ[u]_I. Therefore
lim_jP_{θ+g/j}[u]_I=P_θ[u]_I                 (14)
pointwise, including poles, independently of g. This fixed-data result does not assume or establish survival for an arbitrary changing-data original system.

Finally pullback of a θ-psh function by a modification is μ*θ-psh even when θ is nonclosed. Use local smooth quasi-psh approximation with lower Hessian bound −θ+o(1), pull back each smooth inequality, and pass to the canonical pullback limit. The smooth errors tend to zero on relatively compact sets. All results above use local smooth Hessian bounds, not BMP or numerical mass monotonicity.

notes.summary: Hopf B proved over every ambient competitor: exact submersion ideal pullback and genuine distributional descent yield the scalar envelope identity.
notes.detailedSummary: Fiber Taylor expansion, weighted Parseval and Krull intersection establish ideal pullback for arbitrary holomorphic germs. The entire ambient competitor class is invariant under E, so its envelope is basic. A distributional block-diagonal positivity calculation gives canonical bκ-psh descent, including poles. No basicness restriction on competitors or ambient mass inequality is used.
notes.text:
Proof of the remaining part of B, using n2 and n3.

For any holomorphic submersion p, genuine quasi-psh base weight v and t>0,
I(tp*v)=p^(−1)I(tv)·O.                       (15)
This is an equality for all holomorphic germs upstairs. In product coordinates write F(z,w)=Σ_αf_α(z)w^α. If |F|²exp(−tv(z)) is integrable on a product polydisc, fiber Parseval and Tonelli show every |f_α|²exp(−tv) is integrable on a smaller base polydisc. Each coefficient therefore lies in the coherent ideal J=I(tv). In R=C{z,w}, every finite Taylor truncation lies in JR, giving F∈JR+(w)^N for every N. Krull intersection for the finite R-module R/JR yields F∈JR. Conversely a germ in JR is a finite sum of base generators times holomorphic coefficients, bounded on smaller product polydiscs, so it is integrable. Smooth coordinate volume factors are harmless. Local sections show that equality of pulled ideal classes reflects equality of base classes.

A genuine E-invariant quasi-psh function F descends pointwise to one function v on B, including −∞ on a whole fiber. Product charts and local sections give usc descent; Fubini gives local integrability. Restriction of a local smooth Hessian bound through the section proves v is genuine quasi-psh. If F is bh-psh, put ζ=dw+∂ρ in n2's chart. In the smooth coframe (dξ₁,dξ₂,ζ),
bh+DF=π*(bκ+Dv)+(ib/(2π))ζ∧barζ.
The distributional coefficient matrix is block diagonal, with base block bκ+Dv and positive vertical block. Positivity is invariant under smooth invertible changes of frame: test horizontal lifts annihilated by ζ against nonnegative test functions. Hence bκ+Dv≥0. This includes poles and does not restrict a nonclosed current to a singular slice. Conversely bκ-psh v pulls back to a bh-psh function. Supremum zero is preserved.

Fix normalized v∈PSH(B,bκ) and form U=P_{bh}[π*v]_I. Each element of E preserves h and the seed; change of variables in local integrability sends the entire ambient competitor class bijectively to itself. Thus U is pointwise E invariant. This uses all competitors, without first imposing basicness. By n3 it is a genuine normalized bh-psh function with the exact seed ideals. Write U=π*V. The positivity calculation gives V∈PSH(B,bκ); (15) gives exactly v's ideals. Hence V≤P_{bκ}[v]_I. Conversely any base competitor pulls back to an ambient competitor. Therefore
P_{bh}[π*v]_I=π*P_{bκ}[v]_I.                 (16)
Usc regularization of basic functions commutes with submersion pullback because there are local sections.

Every exceptional constraint is covered: n3 retains ν_F for each prime divisor on each local modification of the threefold. Equation (15) identifies the entire seed ideal sheaf at every positive weight, and (9) identifies every resulting divisorial datum. No claim that threefold valuations are merely base valuations or listed hyperplanes is needed. There is no averaging operation that might weaken ideals. The proof is independent of BMP and ambient mass monotonicity.

notes.summary: G proved: scalar invariance alone canonically constructs the full base system for every positive smooth base perturbation, including nonclosed perturbations.
notes.detailedSummary: Scalar descents share one all-weight ideal class at each parameter. Enveloping any sufficiently small scalar descent defines choice-independent base functions, reproduces all scalar slices and proves compatibility, normalization, concavity and decrease. Metric comparisons give genuine limits equal to the original canonical descent and prove their model property without assuming positive-slice ideal survival.
notes.text:
Proof of G under exactly C's hypotheses. The full original ambient system and its genuine metric-independent limit are hypotheses; a separate transverse system is not assumed.

For ε>0 descend the invariant scalar slice using n4:
Γ_τ^{εh}=π*v_τ^ε, v_τ^ε∈PSH(B,(1+ε)κ), sup v_τ^ε=0.
Equation (16), with b=1+ε, and the ambient model property show that v_τ^ε is an ideal model in (1+ε)κ. For ε≥ε'>0, original compatibility and n3's exact retention imply equality of all ideals of Γ_τ^{εh} and Γ_τ^{ε'h}. Equation (15) reflects these equalities to B. Thus all positive scalar descents have one common all-weight class C_τ. No equality with the limiting class is asserted. Compatibility also descends as actual functions:
v_τ^ε=P_{(1+ε)κ}[v_τ^{ε'}]_I.

For any positive smooth Hermitian ξ on B choose ε>0 with εκ≤ξ and define
Ψ_τ^ξ=P_{κ+ξ}[v_τ^ε]_I.                     (17)
The seed is feasible, so the class is nonempty. All permissible choices have exactly the same ideals and hence the same competitor set. This proves choice independence. The functions are genuine normalized ideal models by n3. If ξ≥ξ', choose one ε with εκ≤ξ'; equation (12) proves compatibility. Using the scalar slice itself as seed gives Ψ_τ^{εκ}=v_τ^ε and the claimed scalar reproduction.

Constancy for τ≤a follows from scalar constancy. Fix ξ and use one permissible ε for the entire parameter interval. The scalar seeds are pointwise decreasing and concave; equations (11)–(13) prove these properties for their envelopes. Explicitly, if 0≤λ≤1 and s,t<c, the combination λΨ_s^ξ+(1−λ)Ψ_t^ξ has every local order at least the order of v_{λs+(1−λ)t}^ε, by scalar concavity. The inequality-envelope description bounds it above by Ψ_{λs+(1−λ)t}^ξ. This checks all exceptional divisors.
